answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake in a shared vault before it may submit work. A random audit samples claims, and a proven duplicate or fabricated identity forfeits that stake; honest agents recover theirs after a waiting period. The stake can be denominated in quartz, while an inlet limits how quickly new identities become eligible, so an attacker must tie up capital and wait for each Sybil rather than minting identities for free. This raises attack cost without assuming that names or network addresses prove uniqueness.
